group_manifest.proof_strategy: For return_wit_1, select the segment-preservation disjunct, destruct nodes, rule out cons using first = sentinel against the nonempty dllseg guard, reduce first_value nil to 0, and cancel the unchanged segment. For return_wit_2, select the full-DLL disjunct, rule out nil using first <> sentinel, obtain that first is the abstract head from the nonempty dllseg branch, prove the first_value equality, combine the sentinel fields as xizi_dll_links, and apply xizi_dll_close. No case_lib helper is needed.

group_entry.proof_strategy: For return_wit_1, select the segment-preservation disjunct, destruct nodes, rule out cons using first = sentinel against the nonempty dllseg guard, reduce first_value nil to 0, and cancel the unchanged segment. For return_wit_2, select the full-DLL disjunct, rule out nil using first <> sentinel, obtain that first is the abstract head from the nonempty dllseg branch, prove the first_value equality, combine the sentinel fields as xizi_dll_links, and apply xizi_dll_close. No case_lib helper is needed.
group_entry.natural_language_proof_strategy: The circular sentinel implementation is abstracted by one predicate fact: an equal segment start/stop represents the empty sequence, while a distinct start/stop forces a nonempty sequence whose head is the start pointer. Use that fact directly, then preserve or close the ownership without mirroring the C conditional.
group_entry.grouping_reason: Same function, complementary sides of the same sentinel/segment case analysis, same case_lib observation, no dependencies, and only two witnesses within max_witnesses_per_group = 12.
